messages:
Sanjay Rao: Hijacking RFC thread briefly 3: I've been prototyping a compact 'assertion bundle' for edge proxies so they can prove a short-lived routing/authority claim without a full control-plane roundtrip. Sketch: signed blob + coarse revocation vector.
Priya Nair: Love the latency wins but need clear semantics: are we granting write authority or only read affinity?
Sanjay Rao: The idea is split: assertion bundles can contain capabilities. Two modes: READ-AFFIX (reads preferred locally) and WRITE-SHORT (timeboxed write authority). WRITE-SHORT requires stricter issuance rules.
Evan (runtime): How small is the blob? We should avoid JWT bloat. Proposal: use a CBOR-like compact payload, base64url-signed by KMS. Payload example:
```
{"lease":"L0-xy","t":1759991234,"exp":1759991294,"caps":"wr:short,rd:preferred","shard":"s-12"}
```
Kara (SRE): Operational constraints: any proxy verification needs to be fast. Offloading verify to edge (nginx/lua) would be ideal. Also: must ship a lightweight revocation vector (bloom + seq) so proxies can drop blacklisted leases quickly.
Priya Nair: What happens on lease collision? Two proxies could have overlapping assertions if network partition delays revocation. We need clear conflict resolution: control-plane sequence number and last-write-wins at shard-level?
Sanjay Rao: Plan: control-plane is the source of truth. Each assertion contains a monotonic epoch and a lease_id. Any request carries (lease_id, epoch). Dataplane rejects lower-epoch writes for the same shard.
Evan (runtime): That still leaves cache coherence problems. If a proxy served a read after evicted but before revocation arrived, clients may see stale results. We'll need cache tombstones keyed by lease_id and a fast invalidation protocol.
Kara (SRE): Tombstone idea sounds ok: when lease moves emit a tombstone event for affected cache keys with TTL matching previous lease. Also add trace tags: trace.region_intent, trace.lease_id, trace.lease_epoch.
Legal-Leah: Compliance checklist: every assertion must be auditable. Log schema must include lease_id, issuing_principal, shard, caps, and an explicit jurisdiction tag. If WRITE-SHORT ever routes writes to a non-home region we must have an approval flag and a retention note.
Priya Nair: Sessions: long-lived streaming connections are hairy. Option A: pin sessions to original lease for a grace window and require new lease for writes. Option B: migrate sessions via a signed handshake between proxies. Which is lower friction?
Evan (runtime): Handshake adds complexity but is more seamless. Minimal handshake: old proxy issues a small transfer token signed by control-plane which new proxy presents. That token is single-use and bounded in time.
Sanjay Rao: Good. We'll prototype transfer token flow: old-proxy -> control-plane -> new-proxy or old-proxy -> new-proxy with control-plane-signed attestation. Simpler is old->control->new to avoid stale proxies making claims.
Kara (SRE): Monitoring: add counters for assertion-verifies, verify-failures, stale-cache-hits, transfer-handshakes, and revocation-lag. Also alert on revocation-lag > 5s for write leases.
Priya Nair: Testing matrix:
- unit: sig/verify + malformed token rejection
- integration: simulate partition with delayed revocation and assert no double-write on shard
- canary: enable READ-AFFIX in eu-central on 2% traffic for non-sensitive tenants
- write-canary: WRITE-SHORT on synthetic tenant in sandbox with operator supervision
deploy-bot: Canary scheduled: eu-central read-affix 2% on 2026-05-12T04:00:00Z. Owners: @Sanjay Rao, @Kara (SRE).
Evan (runtime): Open implementation questions: lease granularity (tenant vs shard-range), assertion TTL (balance risk vs ops churn), and cost of signing at scale. We might batch-sign grants per epoch window.
Legal-Leah: I'll prepare a one-page rubric: when WRITE-SHORT is allowed (e.g., non-PII, pre-approved contracts), required logs, retention period, and data movement notice. Also need a mechanism to record operator approvals attached to lease metadata.
Sanjay Rao: Action items: Priya to pick safe tenants for read-affix canary; Evan to prototype CBOR compact token + nginx verify; Kara to sketch revocation vector proto & monitoring; Leah to produce approval rubric. I'll update the RFC with the assertion bundle format and session transfer options.
Priya Nair: Thanks everyone. Quick note: keep the first canary read-only to avoid regulatory surprises.
Kara (SRE): Agreed. Also let's measure CPU on tls edge during verify peak.
Sanjay Rao: Closing loop: I'll post the RFC patch and ping the channel when ready. :party_popper:
